text: In the bathing house beside the mill, the water around Alyohin turned brown and then dark blue, almost like ink, as the dust of many weeks washed away. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile Ivan Ivanych dived into the millpond with a splash and swam far out in the rain, laughing, diving, and crying out again and again, Oh, my goodness. <break time="0.8s" /> Burkin had to shout several times that it was enough before his friend, still happily splashing among the water lilies, finally climbed out. <break time="0.8s" /> Later, washed and dressed in silk robes and warm slippers, the three men sat in the large drawing room upstairs, where Pelageya served them tea with jam. <break time="0.8s" /> From gilded frames on the walls, portraits of stern generals and gentle ladies looked down on them, and the lamp gave the room a warm, peaceful glow. <break time="0.8s" /> Now that they were comfortable at last, Ivan Ivanych began the story of his younger brother, Nikolai, whose life had been spent in a dull government office. <break time="0.8s" /> The two brothers had grown up in the country, running freely through fields and woods, and that childhood had left them both with a deep love of country life. <break time="0.8s" /> Sitting at his desk year after year, Nikolai dreamed of only one thing, a small farm of his own, with a garden, ducks on a pond, and gooseberry bushes. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan Ivanych did not admire this dream, for he believed that a man needs not six feet of earth, but the whole wide world, where he can freely develop his spirit.
